records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The PR's stated intent is frontend asset optimization, but it adds unrelated concurrency hardening (RWMutex guarding a package-level cache) that is not traceable to any stated requirement in the intent. Scope drift lands in the same diff as an optimization change, so a regression in cache behavior (e.g., a future writer that mutates the returned *dtos.EntryPointAssets in place, which the RWMutex does not protect since the pointer is handed out unlocked) will be attributed to the wrong work item. Reviewers and bisectors tracing 'asset optimization' will hit this concurrency change with no requirement linking it.
records.rationale: The diff adds concurrency hardening around a package-level cache (`entryPointAssetsCacheMu sync.RWMutex` guarding `entryPointAssetsCache`). The getter returns the cached pointer after releasing the read lock (`ret := entryPointAssetsCache; entryPointAssetsCacheMu.RUnlock(); ... return ret`), so any in-place mutation by callers of the returned `*dtos.EntryPointAssets` would not be protected by the mutex. records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cache is only read under RLock but the visible diff never shows a write site inside the newly-acquired write lock, so the added mutex may guard a store that happens outside it. If the (omitted) body below the Lock() writes entryPointAssetsCache without holding it, or if the write path was left unguarded elsewhere, the mutex is decorative and a torn read is still possible; the reviewer cannot verify the invariant from this diff, which itself is a review-safety hazard for a concurrency change.
